items.headline: Sixth edition of Mangaluru Technovanza on Sept 23
items.gist: Mangaluru Technovanza 2026 will be held at Dr TMA Pai International Convention Centre on September 23 under the Beyond Bengaluru initiative by the Electronics, IT and BT Department and Karnataka Digital Economy Mission, expected to bring 600+ delegates, 150+ startups, 40+ global speakers, 50+ global capability centres and 20+ investors to discuss emerging technologies and the cluster’s role as Silicon Beach of India.

items.headline: Kids make eco-friendly Ganesha idols in workshop
items.gist: An eco-friendly clay Ganesha idol-making workshop at Rotary Bala Bhavan, jointly organised by KSPCB Mangaluru, Canara Bank, New Mangalore Port, A J Hospital, CAMP-CO and others, drew about 125 registered children using more than 1,000 kg of clay amid restrictions on Plaster of Paris idols; KSPCB official Dr Manju Rajanna urged natural-clay idols and immersion only at designated tanks.

items.headline: 14 convicted for assault on Bhaskar Shetty murder accused
items.gist: Mangaluru Fast Track Court convicted 14 persons for the 2017 attempt to murder undertrials Navneeth Shetty and Niranjan Bhat inside district prison during the Bhaskar Shetty murder case, with quantum of punishment to be pronounced on September 16; prosecution alleged the accused assaulted the two, struck Shetty with a steel drum and carrom board, and demanded Rs 5 lakh while threatening them to confess to Bhaskar Shetty’s murder.

items.headline: CAMPCO to expand business operations countrywide
items.gist: CAMPCO president S R Satishchandra told the cooperative’s 52nd annual general body meeting at Adyar Garden that it will expand procurement and marketing nationally through agreements with cooperative societies in various states, approved a 14% dividend for arecanut-growing members, and plans an international arecanut conference in Mangaluru in January 2027 plus an arecanut export unit serving markets including Dubai and New Delhi while procuring jackfruit, cashew, cocoa, rubber and black pepper.

items.headline: Mangaluru's unusual four-legged passenger turns heads wherever he goes
items.gist: Auto driver Cyril D'Souza of Kulshekar takes his dog Tuffy on every ride, with the pet sitting beside him as a familiar sight across Mangaluru streets. Cyril told News Trail that Tuffy has become an inseparable companion who prefers being alongside him on short and long rounds through the city.

items.headline: Follow-up drug screening: 38 of 50 students test negative
items.gist: A follow-up drug screening on Thursday found 38 of 50 college students who had initially tested positive now negative after counselling, out of 8,310 students tested from 150 colleges this year where 98 had first tested positive. Authorities said more than 75% of re-tested students reported stopping drug use and advised continued monitoring for the remaining 12.

items.headline: Vivek Alva to participate in conference in Russia
items.gist: Alva's Education Foundation Managing Trustee M. Vivek Alva, along with five other subject experts from India, will participate in the Third International Conference on "Regional-Level Cooperation within BRICS Nations" in Petrozavodsk, Republic of Karelia, Russia, from Tuesday to Thursday, themed "Modern Environmental and Nature Management Issues" and organised by the Karelian Research Centre of the Russian Academy of Sciences in association with the Russian National Committee on BRICS Research.
items.paragraph: Alva's Education Foundation Managing Trustee M. Vivek Alva, along with five other subject experts from India, will participate in the Third International Conference on "Regional-Level Cooperation within BRICS Nations" in Petrozavodsk, Republic of Karelia, Russia, from Tuesday to Thursday, themed "Modern Environmental and Nature Management Issues" and organised by the Karelian Research Centre of the Russian Academy of Sciences in association with the Russian National Committee on BRICS Research. The Indian delegation includes academics from IISc Bengaluru, NIT-K Surathkal, VTU, Chanakya University, and Angadi Institute of Technology and Management; Mr. Alva will speak on "From Awareness to Action: Community-Based Environmental Management in the Western Ghats," showcasing initiatives including Shobhavana and Harish Bhat Pakshivana—the latter recognised under the UN Act to Restore for Climate Action initiative in 2021—and a major initiative covering 46 villages to be brought together through Hasiru Samvada at Alva's Nudisiri–Virasat on January 6 and 7.

items.headline: Tulu Wikipedia marks 10 years, now has about 4,000 articles
items.gist: Tulu Wikipedia, promoted by the Karavali Wikimedians User Group, celebrated its 10th anniversary with activities in Mangaluru on Saturday. President Vishwanath Badikana said it now has about 4,000 articles and 35 active editors, up from a little over 1,000 when it went live on August 6, 2016, at WikiConference India 2016 in Chandigarh, after eight years in incubation as the 23rd Indian language edition of Wikipedia.
items.paragraph: Tulu Wikipedia, promoted by the Karavali Wikimedians User Group, celebrated its 10th anniversary with activities in Mangaluru on Saturday. President Vishwanath Badikana said it now has about 4,000 articles and 35 active editors, up from a little over 1,000 when it went live on August 6, 2016, at WikiConference India 2016 in Chandigarh, after eight years in incubation as the 23rd Indian language edition of Wikipedia. Editors said the project has documented Tulu Nadu's culture, geography, institutions and personalities, and is now documenting living heritage under 'Wiki Loves Tuluvad's Living and Cultural Heritage', with Kanyapu and Sonada Jogi folk performances marking the celebrations.

items.headline: Vande Bharat to Bengaluru should leave in morning, say stakeholders
items.gist: Patrons and associations in coastal Karnataka hope the South Western Railway runtime trial of the Vande Bharat Express between Bengaluru and Mangaluru—leaving Bengaluru in the morning and returning at night—will not set the regular service schedule, saying the train should start from Mangaluru early and return by night for people with official and business work in the State capital. G.
items.paragraph: Patrons and associations in coastal Karnataka hope the South Western Railway runtime trial of the Vande Bharat Express between Bengaluru and Mangaluru—leaving Bengaluru in the morning and returning at night—will not set the regular service schedule, saying the train should start from Mangaluru early and return by night for people with official and business work in the State capital. G. Hanumanth Kamath of Pashchima Karavali Railway Yatri Abhivriddhi Samithi and KCCI president P.B. Ahmed Mudassar said a morning departure around 6 a.m. would mirror the popular Mangaluru–Thiruvananthapuram Vande Bharat pattern; Thursday's trial covered Yeshwantpur–Mangaluru Junction in 7.05 hours and the return in 6.49 hours, with SWR sources telling The Hindu the target is to complete both directions within six hours by speeding up sections where authorised sectional speed is 110 kmph.

items.headline: NSUI alleges violation of rules in M'luru college poll
items.gist: NSUI alleged Students' Union elections at University College, Mangalore on Friday violated state govt guidelines after ABVP-backed candidates won all 37 posts, saying NSUI learnt only on Tuesday that polls would be held Friday despite approaching the vice-chancellor, district minister and principal to follow govt orders. NSUI Dakshina Kannada convener Suhan Alva claimed the higher education secretary said elections held without following the govt order would not be valid and that the V-C had assured polls would not proceed; NSUI said it would condemn the election and demand it be declared invalid, while ABVP's Suvith Shetty said the poll was peaceful.

items.headline: Need for wider reach of Tulu language stressed
items.gist: Karnataka Tulu Sahitya Academy President Taranath Gatti Kapikad, inaugurating the Karavali Wikimedians User Group decennial celebrations in Mangaluru, said Tulu’s literary and cultural wealth confined largely to Dakshina Kannada and Udupi must reach Indian and international audiences through authentic digital documentation; Dr U B Pavanaja said Tulu Wikipedia has gathered 40,000 articles over 10 years, and Wikipedia CEO Bernadette M Meehan praised open repositories across Wikimedia platforms.

items.headline: Udupi’s locked overbridge leaves pedestrians stranded
items.gist: A foot overbridge near Udupi City Municipal Council, built for patients between Urban Primary Health Centre and the old Mother and Child Hospital, stands locked and unused with rust, weeds and blocked staircases as the hospital site changed; social activist Nityananda Olakadu and MLA Yashpal Suvarna urged repair, redesign or relocation, while Commissioner Mahantesh Hangargi said authorities may shift it as a new overbridge near MGM College is set to begin construction next week under a PPP model.

items.headline: 2 arrested for unauthorised rock blasting
items.gist: Manipal police arrested K Govinda Raj (40) of Inna, Karkala, and Shekhappa Chalavadi alias Chandru (28) from Halekatte, Karkala, for alleged unauthorised rock blasting on 1.54 acres of government land in Kukkipalke, Marne village, Udupi taluk on September 5 without departmental permission, registering a case under BNS Sections 288 and 3(5) and Explosives Act Section 9(b) and seizing a tractor with drilling compressor and a car.

items.headline: Protest over insult to Kharge
items.gist: Former minister Jayaprakash Hegde at a Udupi District Congress black-badge protest near Gandhi statue at Ajjarkadu accused the Uttarakhand BJP government of insulting constitutional values by allegedly ordering purification of the stage where AICC president Mallikarjun Kharge spoke, while former minister Vinay Kumar Sorake said the BJP undermines constitutional principles through untouchability; the protest also opposed an FIR against Rahul Gandhi over his protest against the incident.

items.headline: Ivan seeks fact-finding panel on K’rangan report’s impact
items.gist: MLC Ivan D’Souza urged Karnataka MPs to press the Centre for a fact-finding committee on the Kasturirangan Committee report’s impact before any decision, saying the state rejected draft notifications six times, and announced a stakeholders’ meeting in Dakshina Kannada and Udupi within a week ahead of the September 21–23 legislature special session; he also said CM D K Shivakumar will meet ruling and Opposition MLAs on September 18 on coastal employment proposals including CRZ relaxation and demanded Mangalore University conduct direct students’ council elections per government circular.

items.headline: MLC seeks ₹5,000-crore special package for coastal Karnataka at Cabinet meeting
items.gist: MLC and State Congress working president Manjunath Bhandary said he had sought a ₹5,000-crore special economic package for coastal Karnataka to be included in the September 18 Mangaluru Cabinet meeting agenda to improve infrastructure, fisheries, tourism, and higher education and protect coastal culture, and that Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar responded positively and asked the Chief Secretary to include prominent demands.
items.paragraph: MLC and State Congress working president Manjunath Bhandary said he had sought a ₹5,000-crore special economic package for coastal Karnataka to be included in the September 18 Mangaluru Cabinet meeting agenda to improve infrastructure, fisheries, tourism, and higher education and protect coastal culture, and that Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar responded positively and asked the Chief Secretary to include prominent demands. His memorandum also sought an advanced skill development centre, a permanent solution to coastal erosion, upgrading the Brahmavara Agriculture/Horticulture Diploma College as an Agricultural University using 342 acres and ₹20 crore infrastructure, upgrading Mangaluru Fisheries College as a fisheries university, establishing a Karnataka Fisheries Council, developing a modern Aqua Park, raising compensation for fishermen's families who die while fishing from ₹5 lakh to ₹10 lakh, completing the urban ecopark at Pilikula, developing a Karavali religious tourism circuit, and building a coastal parallel road from Talapady to Byndoor.

items.headline: Pranavi Urs targets Asian Games medal, eyes LET and LPGA dream
items.gist: Mysuru golfer Pranavi Urs, part of India's women's Asian Games team with Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar, said consistent rounds of three or four under and solid driving matter more than chasing low numbers in Japan. The 23-year-old LET player, first woman IGPL winner with a 60, said she will treat the Games like any international event and hopes to win a medal.

items.headline: Zero SIR notices: M'luru voters felicitate BLO
items.gist: Voters at booth No 7 of Dakshina Kannada Zilla Panchayat Higher Primary School in Ullal under Mangaluru constituency recorded 100% clean mapping in SIR, with none of the 782 voters — 398 men and 384 women from Kodi, Dota and surrounding areas — served hearing notices or struck off rolls, and they felicitated booth level officer Amrutha Rahul for door-to-door groundwork guiding forms and documents. Amrutha said preliminary work completed in advance meant no notices were needed, in contrast to the rest of Dakshina Kannada where the revision remains rigorous and tense.

items.headline: Being a woman, living in a world of fear
items.gist: Slow redressal, legal lacunae and victim shaming belittle sexual harassment trauma, as illustrated by three cases: a Bengaluru analyst spat on near Kengeri bus stop, Ahmedabad journalist Devanshi Joshi facing rape threats after a 2017 YouTube investigation, and a postgraduate student photographed without consent on Namma Metro. Harassment spans real and virtual worlds, and broadly covers improper conduct causing humiliation or distress.

items.headline: 46 answer scripts of BCom students vanish at BU
items.gist: Answer scripts of 46 BCom students in the Modern Banking subject have gone missing at Bangalore University, leaving fourth-semester pupils awaiting results since April 2025 after January exams whose other results were declared in March. The Syndicate decided to declare results based on marks in other subjects and issue notices to the exam custodian, systems engineer and college principal, but members including Dr H J Jaikrishna demanded a detailed inquiry, citing prior missing-script cases involving 97 students between 2013 and 2023 and alleged mismanagement in the evaluation department.

items.headline: Shopping malls do not require trade licence, rules HC
items.gist: A Karnataka High Court division bench held that shopping malls within BBMP jurisdiction do not require trade licences though individual shops inside do, rejecting BBMP’s demand that Island Star Mall Developers renew trade licence fees for a diesel generator set after the firm had paid Rs 10 lakh and renewed until 2013. The bench said section 354 of the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act requires permission for installation, not annual trade-licence renewal, and that BBMP rendered no inspection service beyond collecting fees while electrical inspector and KSPCB handled certification.

items.headline: Rajanna terms ED raids on Jarkiholi ‘politically motivated’
items.gist: Congress veteran K N Rajanna on Saturday condemned ED raids on properties linked to Public Works Minister Satish Jarkiholi as politically motivated, saying Jarkiholi’s family business has Rs 2,000 crore annual turnover and questioning the significance of seizing Rs 2 crore; he denied reports of quitting Congress over missing an Apex Bank term, said he may or may not contest the next Assembly polls from Madhugiri on a Congress ticket, and deflected questions on CM claims that four to five ministers could face ED raids.

items.headline: 503 child labourers rescued in raids across Bengaluru
items.gist: Joint teams from Bengaluru City Police, Labour Department and Women and Child Development rescued 503 child labourers during surprise inspections at 5,897 locations on Saturday and registered 18 cases under child-labour and juvenile justice laws, with West Division reporting 84 rescues, East 71 and Central 63; a CCB team separately rescued 45 children from 420 locations and registered nine cases following Chief Minister D K Shivakumar’s direction after visiting Yeshwantpur APMC yard.

items.headline: Govt school hours may be changed to avoid B’luru traffic
items.gist: School Education Minister Madhu Bangarappa said he will discuss revising Bengaluru government school timings after teachers reported needing to leave 1.5 hours early yet spending about an hour in traffic to reach schools running 10.30 am–4.30 pm, while private schools operate 8.45 am–3.45 pm; teachers suggested 8.30 am–3.30 pm and Bangarappa said the government is also considering private unaided school staff for State Best Teachers awards.

items.headline: 90% of kidnapping cases reported in B’luru false
items.gist: Data accessed by DH showed about 90% of kidnapping and abduction cases in Bengaluru between 2022 and 2025 were false, including 91.66% in 2022, 86.18% in 2025 and 47.99% in 2026 till August, largely from elopement complaints families later drop; Commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh said minors who elope must be treated as kidnaps and many cases end false when couples return, contributing to low conviction as victims and complainants turn hostile.

items.headline: Proposed ring roads get ‘wider’ development push
items.gist: The Karnataka government will open a four-km-wide development corridor along proposed ring roads in 167 Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities under its Road Network Grid Plan, treating two km on either side as an Impact Zone permitting residential townships, commercial, logistics, educational and tourism projects among others; Chief Minister D K Shivakumar said a new road grid is being formed for mobility, covering cities including Belagavi, Ballari, Chitradurga, Badami, Gauribidanur, Belthangady and Shikaripura.

items.headline: 'I know who complained to ED': Jarkiholi denies foreign funds
items.gist: PWD minister Satish Jarkiholi said he knows who complained against him to the Enforcement Directorate and has informed CM DK Shivakumar, describing the complainant as having Congress links but being a BJP voter, while denying foreign investments and bribery allegations after ED seized Rs 3.4 crore in cash during Sept 9–10 searches at 21 premises in Bengaluru, Belagavi, Gokak and Kolkata under FEMA over suspected undisclosed overseas investments. BJP state president BY Vijayendra questioned whether Congress internal rivalry over the 2028 chief minister's post lay behind the raids, and opposition leader R Ashoka alleged ruling-party functionaries were complaining against colleagues to investigative agencies.

items.headline: Pvt environmental lab faces probe after min's inspection
items.gist: Bengaluru Analytics and Research Laboratory Pvt Ltd faces scrutiny after forest, ecology and environment minister Ramalinga Reddy and senior KSPCB officials conducted a surprise inspection and found multiple irregularities, including operation without valid KSPCB consent after its establishment consent expired in 2025 despite prior MoEFCC permission stating three analysts would be employed when only one was present. Officials found no proper waste-disposal system and alleged waste was discharged into an open pit.

items.headline: Medical colleges to adopt taluk hospitals
items.gist: The state govt has directed every government and private medical college to adopt one taluk hospital, one Community Health Centre and one Primary Health Centre under a Health Department circular issued Thursday, as part of the chief minister's 100-day programme to deploy gynaecologists, anaesthesiologists, paediatricians and orthopaedic surgeons in rural areas. items.headline: Can Cabinet panel take school fees’ bull run by the horns?
items.gist: A Cabinet sub-committee on students’ issues includes regulating private-institution fees among its terms of reference, but Karnataka lacks a dedicated fee-regulation committee and courts have struck down rigid fee-fixing, including the 2023 Dharwad bench ruling against section 48 of the Karnataka Education Act for unaided schools, an order the government has appealed. Private school associations accept regulation of fees above 20% excess but reject fee formulas, while parents’ groups cite Tamil Nadu’s judge-headed commission model and Minister Madhu Bangarappa said legal issues must be resolved; CM D K Shivakumar warned institutions charging over Rs 50,000 annually to adopt village government schools or face fee caps.

items.headline: Protest against limiting 'Vande Mataram' rendition
items.gist: BJP State president B.Y. Vijayendra said on Saturday the party will organise a five-day padayatra across all 224 Assembly constituencies in Karnataka from Tuesday to protest the State government's decision to limit Vande Mataram to two stanzas at official events.

items.headline: K'taka considers bringing back physical marks cards
items.gist: The higher education department is considering revoking its circular that stopped issuing physical marks cards after vice-chancellors at a Karnataka State Higher Education Council meeting with minister Basavaraj Rayareddi flagged student difficulties with DigiLocker-only records, including rejection by foreign universities and corporates. The 2023-24 budget had switched fully to digital marks cards to curb fake certificates; a proposed hybrid system would issue both physical and digital cards with online verification, uniform minimum and maximum printing rates across universities, and a committee to recommend security features within a week.

items.headline: Fewer ATHLETES, same EXPECTATIONS
items.gist: Twenty-three Karnataka sportspersons, most making their Asian Games debut, are part of India’s 500-plus contingent for the 20th Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, from September 19 — down from roughly 37 at Hangzhou four years ago. Medal hopes include pole-vault record holder Sindhushree G, 400m hurdler Yashas P, relay runners Unnathi Aiyappa, Sneha SS and Poovamma MR, Mangaluru shuttler Ayush Shetty, golfers Aditi Ashok and Pranavi Urs, swimmers led by Srihari Nataraj, hockey goalkeeper Mohith HS, and shooter Tilottama Sen; Deputy Chief Minister G Parameshwara announced Rs 5 lakh each for state athletes at the Commonwealth Games and Asiad, atop Rs 35 lakh, Rs 25 lakh and Rs 15 lakh for gold, silver and bronze.

items.headline: Pipers, Grandmasters reach final
items.gist: On a dramatic Saturday in the Global Chess League in Bengaluru, Alpine APL Pipers and Ganges Grandmasters — both on 18 points — advanced to the Sunday final after the top three teams chasing a final berth all lost to bottom-placed sides; FYERS American Gambits and CheQ Mumba Masters (15 points each) will play for third place. Gambits needed at least nine game points against Masters but fell 11-6 after Nihal Sarin squandered a winning position, while Magnus Carlsen’s Pipers lost 11-6 to Triveni Continental Kings and Grandmasters lost 9-7 to PBG Alaskan Knights despite needing only one game point to qualify.

items.headline: Srinath's delicate balancing act of coaching two sides
items.gist: GM Srinath Narayanan, coach of FYERS American Gambits at the Bengaluru Global Chess League, will switch to India’s national team at the Chess Olympiad in Samarkand from September 16, working with Arjun Erigaisi, R Praggnanandhaa, Nihal Sarin, D Gukesh and Vidit Gujrathi after coaching an international Gambits squad that includes Uzbek icon Javokhir Sindarov. Srinath said he and Sindarov maintain clear boundaries on personal chess matters while functioning as one unit, ahead of Sindarov leading Uzbekistan and later facing Gukesh in the World Chess Championship.

items.headline: Ashique finds his wings again with Blues
items.gist: Kerala winger Ashique Kuruniyan, 29, says returning to Bengaluru FC after injury-hit years at Mohun Bagan — including an ACL tear playing for India against Iraq in September 2023 — has restored his joy under coach Pep Munoz ahead of friendlies against Panama, Brazil and Uruguay. Head coaches Renedy Singh and Munoz have kept him as the first choice on the left flank as he prepares to feature again for India.

items.headline: The gallery that grew with the city
items.gist: Deepa Natarajan Lobo recounts ophthalmologist Dr Premilla Baid founding Gallery Sumukha in Bengaluru in 1996 after charity shows and early Chittrovanu Mazumdar and Kolkata artist exhibitions, moving from a family outhouse to Alliance Française and Wilson Garden in 1999. Thirty years on, Sumukha hosted artists from K G Subramanyan and Gulammohammed Sheikh to younger names, Peter Nagy-curated shows, and international fairs, with Dr Premilla urging welcoming spaces where visitors discover art without pressure to buy.

items.headline: HC orders SIT probe into 16-year-old accident case
items.gist: The Karnataka High Court Dharwad bench ordered an SIT probe into a 2009 road accident case, suspecting manipulation to claim insurance compensation, while dismissing appellant Giridhar Neelakantha Pai's appeal and imposing Rs 10,000 costs. The court noted Giridhar lacked a valid licence, inconsistencies in hospital records, and possible collusion among complainants to defraud the insurer.

items.headline: Bengaluru girl missing for over seven months traced to Kanakapura using Aadhaar OTP
items.gist: An 18-year-old second-year PU student missing from Bengaluru's Vidyaranyapura since January 31 was traced to Kanakapura taluk after CID investigators linked her Aadhaar use to an OTP on her husband's phone. The girl, found married and pregnant, was handed to her parents after a habeas corpus petition and High Court proceedings.

items.headline: Court dismisses IPS officer's plea in PSI assault case

items.headline: Actor Prakash Raj announces campaign across 10 districts in Karnataka
items.gist: Prakash Raj said he will conduct a social audit of the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls across 10 districts from September 20 to 30, visiting booths to compare EC records with deleted names and gathering evidence from affected voters. He alleged the SIR was a conspiracy, cited a Mandya woman who voted in 36 elections but now faces deletion, and said evidence would be taken to courts by October 15.

items.headline: 3,200 agriculture quota seats available for farmers' children in Karnataka

items.headline: DyCM warns caste census could be a 'meaningless' count
items.gist: Deputy CM G Parameshwara warned that an open-ended 2027 Census caste methodology could fragment communities into thousands of duplicate entries and undermine social justice data. He urged the Centre to develop standardised OBC codes like SC/ST lists, consult states including Karnataka from its Social and Educational Survey experience, and produce accurate data for reservation and welfare policy.

items.headline: Over 250 clips on mobile, pendrive seized from Prajwal
items.gist: Forensic analysis of the mobile phone and pen drive seized from the prison cell where former MP Prajwal Revanna was lodged during a CCB raid found over 147 video clips on the phone and more than 100 videos on the pen drive, reportedly including porn clips, OTT series and movies. Revanna has reportedly told investigators that he used the phone mainly for making calls, admitted contacting his mother through a phone used by one of her maids rather than calling her directly, and claimed the phone was circulated among several prisoners on a rotational basis so he did not know who downloaded the material.
items.paragraph: Forensic analysis of the mobile phone and pen drive seized from the prison cell where former MP Prajwal Revanna was lodged during a CCB raid found over 147 video clips on the phone and more than 100 videos on the pen drive, reportedly including porn clips, OTT series and movies. Revanna has reportedly told investigators that he used the phone mainly for making calls, admitted contacting his mother through a phone used by one of her maids rather than calling her directly, and claimed the phone was circulated among several prisoners on a rotational basis so he did not know who downloaded the material. Police are scrutinising call records and are likely to issue notices to persons contacted from the device; Revanna is said to have used the mobile in jail for regular and video calls and reportedly paid around ₹1 lakh to get the phone.

items.headline: Sugar price spike revives farmers' demand for jaggery-based ethanol units
items.gist: A surge in sugar prices ahead of the festive season — Gowri-Ganesha, Dasara and Deepavali — amid reports of sugarcane diversion for ethanol has revived Karnataka farmers' demand that jaggery and grain-based units be allowed to produce ethanol. State Sugarcane Growers' Association president Kurubur Shanthakumar said ethanol procurement at around ₹65 a litre could substantially raise growers' incomes, noting Karnataka produces about 600 lakh tonnes of sugarcane annually but only 30 to 40 lakh tonnes go to some 15,000 jaggery units.
items.paragraph: A surge in sugar prices ahead of the festive season — Gowri-Ganesha, Dasara and Deepavali — amid reports of sugarcane diversion for ethanol has revived Karnataka farmers' demand that jaggery and grain-based units be allowed to produce ethanol. State Sugarcane Growers' Association president Kurubur Shanthakumar said ethanol procurement at around ₹65 a litre could substantially raise growers' incomes, noting Karnataka produces about 600 lakh tonnes of sugarcane annually but only 30 to 40 lakh tonnes go to some 15,000 jaggery units. Speakers at a recent Bengaluru seminar cited maize prices crossing ₹3,200 a quintal from below ₹2,800 before ethanol expansion, and said Karnataka's 56 ethanol units rank third nationally with about 135 crore litres produced annually.

items.headline: CM to hear people from regions affected by Kasturirangan report
items.gist: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, who will chair a Cabinet meeting at Praja Soudha in Mangaluru from 10 a.m.
items.paragraph: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, who will chair a Cabinet meeting at Praja Soudha in Mangaluru from 10 a.m. on September 18, will hold public meetings in Udupi, Shivamogga, and Chikkamagaluru districts on September 18 and 19 to hear from people in areas that could be affected by the Kasturirangan Committee report, travelling by helicopter to Hebri (3 p.m. on September 18), Tirthahalli (10 a.m. on September 19), and Balehonnur (1 p.m. on September 19) before returning to Bengaluru that evening. Meanwhile, MLC Ivan D'Souza said he will interact with people affected by the report ahead of the September 21–23 special legislature session, noting that although the State government has rejected the report eight times, the Union government has been pressuring southern states to accept it and that as many as seven districts would be impacted.

items.headline: Worker attacked
items.gist: The Whitefield police have booked a woman who allegedly assaulted a civic worker with a stone after he asked her not to throw a used tea cup on the roadside on Pattandur Agrahara Main Road on Friday. The incident occurred on Kuvempu Road, where the woman, identified as Vaidehi, a private firm employee, was with her male friend after having tea; when the civic worker asked them to put the cup in a dustbin instead of littering, Vaidehi allegedly abused him and hurled a stone at him, with witnesses claiming she appeared to be under the influence of alcohol, after which a police team reached the spot and detained Vaidehi and her friend.

items.headline: Fake doctors will face strict legal action, DHOs and THOs could be held accountable: Health Minister
items.gist: Health and Family Welfare Minister U.T. Khader said in Dharwad on Saturday that stringent legal action would be taken against fake doctors and that District Health Officers and Taluk Health Officers could also be held accountable if such practitioners were found operating in their jurisdictions, with an official order to be issued shortly.
items.paragraph: Health and Family Welfare Minister U.T. Khader said in Dharwad on Saturday that stringent legal action would be taken against fake doctors and that District Health Officers and Taluk Health Officers could also be held accountable if such practitioners were found operating in their jurisdictions, with an official order to be issued shortly. Speaking to presspersons, he said if a fake doctor is found during an inspection, the concerned DHO will be held responsible; he also said the government had prohibited sale of paan masala and gutka containing tobacco and nicotine, was conducting inspections on food adulteration and urging consumers to report poor hygiene via a QR code system, and described Enforcement Directorate action against Minister Satish Jarkiholi as part of "targeted politics," alleging a large proportion of ED cases were aimed at Congress leaders while similar action was not taken against BJP leaders.

items.headline: Solar power to reach 1,900 anganwadis
items.gist: The Department of Women and Child Development has partnered with the SELCO Foundation to provide solar power to 1,900 anganwadi centres across Karnataka, focusing on remote and underserved areas, under a Memorandum of Understanding signed by WCD Director Mahesh Babu and SELCO Foundation Director Huda Jaffer. The initiative, estimated to cost about ₹16 crore, aims to improve basic facilities for early childhood care, preschool education, nutrition and health services, with training for anganwadi staff on solar system use and the Soura e-Mitra application to report faults and access technical support.

items.headline: KITU flags deletion of women's night-shift safeguards; Labour Department says OSH Code covers them
items.gist: The Karnataka State IT/ITeS Employees' Union has condemned the omission of several clauses of the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments Act through an amendment published in the Gazette on September 4, saying it removes safety and security measures for women on night shifts, including mandatory driver verification, authorised pick-up and drop routes, confidentiality of contact details, security guards, and emergency mechanisms. KITU demanded immediate withdrawal of amendments deleting Section 25(1)(h)–(o) and restoration of all statutory safeguards.
items.paragraph: The Karnataka State IT/ITeS Employees' Union has condemned the omission of several clauses of the Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments Act through an amendment published in the Gazette on September 4, saying it removes safety and security measures for women on night shifts, including mandatory driver verification, authorised pick-up and drop routes, confidentiality of contact details, security guards, and emergency mechanisms. KITU demanded immediate withdrawal of amendments deleting Section 25(1)(h)–(o) and restoration of all statutory safeguards. Labour Department sources said the provisions are now covered under the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, as the Shops Act applies only to establishments employing fewer than 10 people while larger establishments fall under OSH.

items.headline: 'As long as I'm scoring runs, I'm happy'
items.gist: Karnataka batter Devdutt Padikkal scored two centuries in three innings on India's recent Test tour of Sri Lanka, amassing 328 runs and winning Player-of-the-Series honours after returning to the Test squad after nearly two years. The 26-year-old, who amassed 543 runs in six Ranji Trophy games last season, said domestic cricket makes a player tougher and that game time provides first-hand experience on how to model one's game, and he is looking forward to leading India-A against Australia-A later this month after captaining Karnataka from mid-season last year.

items.headline: Union: Rollback of safety norms for women risky
items.gist: The Karnataka State IT/ITeS Employees Union has opposed the state government's decision to remove statutory safety and security measures for women working night shifts, saying the move could increase risks and dilute employer accountability. Deleted provisions had required safer late-night commutes through driver verification, route monitoring, protection of women's details, and rules on first pick-up and last drop-off.

items.headline: 4-day crackdown: 800 children rescued from 17k workplaces
items.gist: Police rescued nearly 800 children working in hotels, garages, shops and other establishments after raids at nearly 17,000 premises across 962 police station limits in Karnataka following CM DK Shivakumar's directive, triggered after he reportedly saw a child labourer at Yeshwantpur APMC Yard on Sept 8. Bengaluru accounted for 503 rescues from 5,897 premises inspected under 188 police stations, with children paid Rs 10,000–Rs 16,000 monthly; FIRs were filed in five cases, 54 children handed to Child Welfare Committees, and rescued children included migrants from Bihar, Assam, West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Jharkhand and Nepal.

items.headline: Min: Will look into changing school timings
items.gist: School education and literacy minister Madhu Bangarappa said the state govt will look into changing school timings after MLC Puttanna raised the demand, citing Bengaluru's worsening traffic congestion affecting students' and teachers' daily commutes. Bangarappa said govt would consult various departments before deciding, and that the state was considering extending state-level teacher awards to deserving teachers in private schools.

items.headline: Making A Difference: Workshops Shape Greener Ganesha Festival
items.gist: Ahead of Ganesh Chaturthi on Monday, citizen groups, lake activists and RWAs across Bengaluru are running free clay idol-making workshops to move families away from Plaster-of-Paris idols toward natural clay; groups such as Benniganahalli Kere Community Development Trust and HSR Citizen Forum have held such sessions for years. On Saturday actress Ragini Dwivedi joined a Bharatinagar Residents Forum demo in Cox Town, and city immersion arrangements include 659 mobile tanks across five corporations with single-window permit centres; organisers say making idols themselves helps children understand the environmental impact of festival choices.

items.headline: Safe travels: RPF ups security for festive rush
items.gist: Following overcrowding at city railway stations from Friday evening, South Western Railway's Bengaluru division said additional Railway Protection Force personnel will be deployed at major stations, platforms, circulating areas and vulnerable locations during the Gauri Ganesha festival, with the RPF dog squad conducting anti-sabotage and explosive detection checks. In coordination with GRP and other agencies, RPF will maintain CCTV surveillance and crowd management; passengers are advised to remain vigilant, safeguard belongings and report suspicious activity to helpline 139 or nearest RPF/GRP personnel.

items.headline: Opinions sought on bus fare revision by RTCs
items.gist: The Karnataka Public Transport Fare Regulatory Committee has invited suggestions and objections by Sept 21 on revising bus fares for KSRTC, BMTC, NWKRTC and KKRTC, citing rising diesel and fuel prices, higher staff salaries and operating costs; submissions can be sent to the committee chairperson at Shanti Nagar, Bengaluru, or via https://ksrtc.org/fare_revision_feedback/. The four corporations' combined liabilities stood at Rs 8,095.5 crore as of May 31, 2026, and they have also sought Rs 5,418.6 crore from govt as reimbursement under the Shakti scheme; bus fares were last increased by 15% in January 2025.

items.headline: Anticipatory bail for Munirathna
items.gist: A special court for elected representatives has granted anticipatory bail till Sept 15 to RR Nagar MLA Munirathna Naidu in a criminal case registered for threatening a woman, who had lodged a complaint against the MLA and seven others accusing them of threatening her to withdraw a rape case she filed in 2021 against Ravi Shankar, a close associate of the MLA. The court said the petitioner shall be released if arrested upon executing a personal bond of Rs 2 lakh.

items.headline: 2 rob woman of gold chain
items.gist: Two bike-borne miscreants snatched a 55g two-strand gold mangalya chain worth over Rs 7.5 lakh from Shivaranjini, 25, around 8am on Nayandahalli Metro Layout rail-underpass road in west Bengaluru as she walked to work at a fuel station; the pillion rider in a red jacket grabbed the chain after approaching from behind. She held on but suffered neck pain, was treated at a hospital and then approached police after passersby alerted them.

items.headline: PLOGGING TO BOTANICAL ART, CITIZENS TURN UP FOR CITY
items.gist: The Times of India's #IamBengaluru – Volunteer for Parks campaign's fifth week began Saturday with a jog-and-plogging activity at Jakkur Park led by Jalaposhan Trust, a plogging and waste-segregation drive at RBI Layout Park No 2 by Youth for Seva that cumulatively collected 10 large bags of plastic waste, and a botanical art workshop at Koramangala 5th Block Park mentored by Pavithra S of Kiria Arts. National Public School Rajajinagar students demonstrated textile-waste segregation under Project Evara, and participants said the initiative helps reconnect Bengalureans with parks amid rapid digital-era change.

items.headline: Rapido driver flees with rider's phone, seeks 18k
items.gist: Trideep Debnath, 25, filed a complaint at Madiwala police station after Rapido rider Ashutosh Kumar, who arrived on a white scooter instead of booked vehicle KA-01-HX-7232, fled with his Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra worth around Rs 50,000 during a ride booked at 5.54am on Sept 6 from Narayanappa Garden 4th Cross to Marathahalli when Debnath stepped off at a Madiwala fuel station. The accused later contacted Debnep's sister via WhatsApp demanding Rs 18,000 to return the phone, threatening to destroy or sell it outside Karnataka, and sent a UPI payment scanner.

items.headline: Family alleges social boycott over roadside structure
items.gist: A Scheduled Caste family from Kuruvangi village in Chikkamagaluru taluk has alleged social boycott after objecting to Venkatesh constructing a metal-sheet structure and installing an iron pole in a drain leading to welder KM Rajesh's house, obstructing movement; Rajesh told Chikkamagaluru Rural police Venkatesh attempted to assault him and his mother when questioned and that three high-voltage lines above pose a safety risk. items.headline: 'If only forests had Wi-Fi': Bittu Tabahi stunned by waste at Turahalli
items.gist: Madhya Pradesh environment activist Surendra Singh Choudhary, known as Bittu Tabahi, joined AN Yellappa Reddy and volunteers in a Clean Up Turahalli drive Saturday along the Banashankari 6th Stage periphery of Turahalli Reserve Forest, organised by The Indian Garage Co with Indus Herbs and GBA support, removing over two tonnes of legacy waste including poultry waste, sanitary waste, dog carcasses, medical waste and plastic over nearly four hours from 8am, requiring a backhoe. Bittu, a 21-year-old BSc student who spent Rs 30,000 cleaning three ghats of Ajnar river in Madhya Pradesh, said he expected Bengaluru's green spaces to be litter-free and remarked that if forests had Wi-Fi people might treat them with more regard.

items.headline: Catch-22 for foresters as DKS warns against excessive action
items.gist: At the National Forest Martyrs' Day event at Aranya Bhavan on Friday, CM DK Shivakumar told forest officials the public do not accept them as readily as police officers and urged friendly relations with fringe communities, saying encroachments must be resolved legally without unnecessary pressure and that officials should not obstruct development projects or act excessively. A retired principal chief conservator of forests said the remarks could leave field staff caught between accusations of over-enforcement and being soft on encroachment, especially along forest boundaries where cultivation and construction expand into forest land.

items.headline: Lovers found hanging on K'buragi hill

items.headline: Vroom to volt
items.gist: Bengaluru buyers weighing an EV this festive season should look beyond design and fuel savings, experts say. Sunil Pai, MD and CEO of a multi-brand automotive retail group, cited FAME-scheme momentum, 500 km-plus ranges, fast-charging on highways, and EVs’ tech and comfort edge; electric two-wheelers lead local adoption for affordability and city use.
items.paragraph: Bengaluru buyers weighing an EV this festive season should look beyond design and fuel savings, experts say. Sunil Pai, MD and CEO of a multi-brand automotive retail group, cited FAME-scheme momentum, 500 km-plus ranges, fast-charging on highways, and EVs’ tech and comfort edge; electric two-wheelers lead local adoption for affordability and city use. Abin Varghese, director of an electric mobility firm, advised matching real-world range to your commute, securing home or workplace charging—overnight charging works best—and evaluating battery tech, warranty, OTA updates, service network, spare parts and roadside assistance rather than buying solely to cut fuel costs; a test drive should assess torque, regenerative braking, modes and ergonomics.

items.headline: Xi and Modi welcome 'steady progress' in ties
items.gist: India and China expressed commitment to a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable resolution of the boundary question, proceeding from the political perspective of overall bilateral relations and the long-term interests of the two peoples, the External Affairs Ministry said after the leaders' meeting. A Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs statement said both sides should pursue progress on bilateral relations and the boundary question in parallel, ensuring each supports the other and maintaining peace and tranquillity in border areas.
items.paragraph: India and China expressed commitment to a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable resolution of the boundary question, proceeding from the political perspective of overall bilateral relations and the long-term interests of the two peoples, the External Affairs Ministry said after the leaders' meeting. A Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs statement said both sides should pursue progress on bilateral relations and the boundary question in parallel, ensuring each supports the other and maintaining peace and tranquillity in border areas. Mr. Xi arrived with a large delegation for a two-day visit and was driven to Bharat Mandapam amid tight security; the two leaders agreed to continue expanding common ground in resolving regional and global issues while addressing challenges. Speaking at the summit on West Asia, Mr. Xi said the war has inflicted serious losses on people across the region and Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning called for a political settlement, with Mr. Xi saying China would work with fellow BRICS members to bring peace and tranquillity to the Middle East and that India and China, as key Global South members, bear significant responsibilities in world affairs.

items.headline: NIA court issues arrest warrant against LeT chief
items.gist: A special National Investigation Agency court in Jammu issued a non-bailable arrest warrant against Lashkar-e-Taiba founder Hafiz Muhammad Saeed in a case related to providing weapons, money and directions to terrorists operating in the Kashmir Valley, after the NIA moved under Section 75 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita alleging he operates from Pakistan and is deliberately evading arrest. The case stems from the arrest this year of Mohammad Naqeeb Bhat in Ganderbal with a Chinese grenade and 15 live rounds, linked to LeT/The Resistance Front; the agency also searched 10 locations in Kupwara, Kulgam, Bandipora, Baramulla and Sopore in the Zakoora case and said it found linkages between Pakistan-based LeT handlers and local associates.

items.headline: Farmers’ alliance seeks statute on seed rights
items.gist: Bharat Beej Swaraj Manch urged legislation ensuring farmers’ natural seed rights are not subordinate to breeders’ rights under the PPV&FR Act, a month after the Supreme Court in Kavita Kuruganti vs PepsiCo India agreed with the Delhi High Court that farmers claiming protection under the Act may do so while PepsiCo retains legal remedies if its registered potato variety rights are infringed.

items.headline: Maharashtra: ST discontent wells up during Ganeshotsav
items.gist: Scheduled Tribe grievances over Forest Rights Act implementation, hostel conditions, PESA appointments and Dhangar ST inclusion demands persist after the 2018 Nashik-Mumbai farmers’ march, with recent snakebite deaths of three tribal ashram hostel girls in Gadchiroli and a fever death in Palghar intensifying protests Rahul Gandhi amplified; the Fadnavis government formed a high-level recruitment review committee after Pune and Nashik agitations, a 17-day Manjari hostel fast ending after Tribal Development Minister Ashok Uike’s assurances, and Sakal Adivasi Vidyarthi Andolan Kruti Samiti planning a September 15–20 Nashik-Mumbai march during Ganeshotsav.

items.headline: Tata Sons can't surrender NBFC licence: RBI
items.gist: The Reserve Bank of India has rejected Tata Sons' application to surrender its Non-Banking Finance Company licence, saying the application "cannot be acceded to" and asking the Tata Group holding company to prepare for an immediate public listing, putting an end to years of uncertainty. Tata Sons had applied for de-registration as it was majority-owned by charitable trusts and was not mobilising public funds, but the RBI included it in the list of 17 large upper-layer NBFCs for 2026-27 subject to enhanced regulatory requirements and mandatory listing within three years of identification.

items.headline: EC meets both Trinamool Congress factions, seeks more documents from Ritabrata camp
items.gist: The Election Commission met both Trinamool Congress factions — Mamata Banerjee-led and Ritabrata Banerjee-led — over claims to the party name and 'joda ghash phool' symbol ahead of October 6 Assembly bypolls in Nandigram and Rejinagar, for which nominations opened Wednesday and close on September 16. Ritabrata claims support of over 65 Trinamool MLAs of 80 in the 294-member Assembly; the EC sought additional documents from his faction and, citing Shiv Sena precedent, sources said the symbol may be frozen temporarily, while Mamata's delegation insisted there was no dispute and said defectors who received ₹25 lakh each to contest elections five months ago were traitors.

items.headline: Amid ED action on aide, Rawat offers to quit two Cong. posts
items.gist: Former Uttarakhand Chief Minister Harish Rawat offered to step down as executive member of the Uttarakhand Pradesh Congress Committee and as permanent invitee to the Congress Working Committee after the Enforcement Directorate searched the house of his former officer on special duty Chandan Singh Jeena over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations during Rawat's tenure. Rawat said no weakness should enter the party's anti-corruption struggle on his account and called the ED action a narrative-building attempt; Uttarakhand Congress president Ganesh Godiyal said the 2016 examination was cancelled and investigated under Rawat's government and questioned why the Centre acted after 11 years.

items.headline: Hyderabad man loses Rs 3.35 cr to investment scam
items.gist: Telangana Cyber Security Bureau registered a case after a man reportedly lost Rs 3.35 crore over about 55 days to a fraudster who contacted him via a dating app, built trust on WhatsApp, and lured him into a fake Meta-related investment app showing apparent profits before demanding more money when he tried to withdraw, citing a lowered credit score.

items.headline: US finalises levies on solar cell imports from India
items.gist: The US Department of Commerce on Friday finalised anti-dumping margins of 123.04% for Indian producers, 94.36% for Indonesia and 65.43% for Laos, and countervailing duty rates of 126.09% for India, 73.2–173.7% for Indonesia and 82.03–153.67% for Laos on crystalline silicon photovoltaic cells, following complaints of unfair subsidies harming American solar manufacturing; the US International Trade Commission will decide by October 14 whether to issue duty orders by November 2 or terminate the probe.

items.headline: India eye record eighth title
items.gist: Seven-time champions India will look to Shafali Verma (168 runs, two fifties, tournament’s leading scorer) and Deepti Sharma (11 wickets, joint top with Chamari Athapaththu) when they face Sri Lanka in the Women’s T20 Asia Cup final in Dubai on Sunday. Harmanpreet Kaur’s side remain wary after Sri Lanka’s eight-wicket win in the 2024 final and their semifinal recovery from 5/2 and 33/4 to chase 131 against Pakistan, while India’s fielding concerns persist with nine dropped catches in four matches.

items.headline: India brace for tricky Afg test
items.gist: India face a selection dilemma between Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s aggression and Sanju Samson’s experience in the first T20I against Afghanistan in New Delhi on Sunday, with both possibly playing if Ishan Kishan is ruled out after a back scare. Shreyas Iyer’s side, preparing for the Asian Games, will test themselves against Rashid Khan, Noor Ahmed and Mujeeb ur Rahman in a three-match series where India lead the bilateral T20I head-to-head 8-0 with one no-result in nine meetings.

items.headline: Amount of cricket the main reason for injuries: Iyer

items.headline: At 90, veteran artist Gulammohammed Sheikh continues to confront violence, dogmatism and injustice, turning our everyday realities into works that speak
items.gist: Kavita Chowdhury profiles Gulammohammed Sheikh ahead of his 90th birthday, covering the Kolkata retrospective *Handprints/Mindprints* of over 100 prints curated by Pushpamala N, works confronting riots from 1969 Baroda to post-Babri violence and digital *Mappamundi: Troubled Terrains*, and his self-description as “artist-activist.” Sheikh quotes Kabir and Gandhi as counterpoints to normalised violence and says he fully supports the “brave” Gen Z non-violent protests at Jantar Mantar.

items.gist: Rahul Jha allegedly killed his wife Geeta and daughters Nandini, 23, Radhika, 18, and a 14-year-old at their Jaipur Kardhani home, then served tea to his elderly father the next morning before fleeing. Police recovered the stone used in the attack; Jha, a share trader who had borrowed Rs 25,000 days earlier, is being sought as financial distress and family disputes are probed.

items.headline: GDP BOOM, PEOPLE'S GLOOM
items.gist: India's GDP grew 7.8% in April-June 2026, adding nearly Rs 5.89 lakh crore, while the RBI's FCNR(B) scheme drew a record $136 billion (about Rs 12 lakh crore), but sugar has jumped 30-40% to Rs 61-68 a kg across cities and milk, vegetables and eggs are 15-35% costlier. Muralidhar Swaminathan writes that headline growth and forex inflows have not eased the common citizen's cost-of-living squeeze.

items.headline: Modi, Xi 'express commitment' to resolving border issue
items.gist: PM Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping agreed to work towards a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable boundary resolution during their meeting on the BRICS summit sidelines in New Delhi, India's foreign ministry said. items.headline: Apology
items.gist: The Hindu deeply regrets the publication in its Delhi, Mohali, and North India editions of an offensive front-page advertisement titled "What is Dera Sacha Sauda? (Facts vs Fiction)" alleging, among other things, that there was a conspiracy against the convicted rapist, Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh, head of the Dera Sacha Sauda, by "drug mafias and forces opposed to the Dera." The Hindu tenders its unconditional apology to its readers for publishing this deeply offensive advertisement.

Principal Scientific Adviser Ajay Kumar Sood launched the initiative in New Delhi on Friday, with participating institutions exchanging a Memorandum of Agreement; it operates through AMTZ, the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser, FICCI, and the Science & Technology Cluster.

items.headline: Arms theft case: police to seek custody of ex-Havildar

items.headline: 1.4 lakh MBBS seats available in 836 colleges after revision
items.gist: The National Medical Commission has revised the MBBS seat matrix for the 2026-27 academic year, cautioning medical colleges and counselling authorities against admitting students beyond regulator-approved intake. The updated matrix lists 1,40,214 MBBS seats across 836 medical colleges — 63,971 in 391 government colleges and 76,243 in 445 private colleges — incorporating permissions for new colleges and increased intake at existing ones; the NMC said the matrix is not necessarily final.

items.headline: Fugitive gangster extradited from Moldova: Punjab Police
items.gist: Punjab Police said fugitive criminal Amritpal Singh, alias Amrit Dalam, a key operative of the Jaggu Bhagwanpuria gang, was extradited from the Republic of Moldova with assistance from Central agencies. Wanted in multiple cases of murder, attempt to murder, UAPA, Arms Act and narcotics offences, his return marks the first extradition secured by Punjab Police from a European country, Director-General of Police Gaurav Yadav said, calling it a breakthrough against transnational organised crime.

items.headline: Air India pilot found dead in hotel; police rule out foul play
items.gist: An Air India pilot in Delhi for Boeing 787 conversion training died after being found unconscious in his hotel room in Vasant Kunj during a layover; he had checked in on Thursday and was found dead the next evening. The pilot, who had worked with Air India Express, was undergoing conversion training for wide-body Boeing 787 aircraft; a post-mortem was conducted at Safdarjung Hospital and the final cause of death awaits the medical opinion, while police said they were not suspecting foul play.

items.headline: Body of Jaish terrorist found in Doda; M4 rifle recovered
items.gist: Jammu and Kashmir Police recovered the body of a Pakistani Jaish-e-Mohammed terrorist from the upper reaches of Chenab Valley's Doda district on Saturday. items.headline: Ladakh talks fruitful, but Wangchuk, others misled people: ex-MP
items.gist: Former BJP MP from Ladakh Thupstan Chhewang said September 9 talks between Ladakhi civil society leaders, the Union Ministry of Home Affairs and the UT administration were "fruitful", countering the disappointment expressed by Leh Apex Body, Kargil Democratic Alliance and activist Sonam Wangchuk. Ladakh Chief Secretary Ashish Kundra had proposed a sui generis model under Article 371 with legislative, executive and financial powers, but LAB and KDA called the meeting a waste of time; Chhewang said positive consensus points were not brought before the public and criticised Wangchuk's reported call for renewed agitation with an ultimatum.

items.headline: Delhi slum covered with large sheets amid summit
items.gist: With the BRICS summit under way in Delhi, Coolie camp, a slum settlement in south Delhi's Vasant Vihar housing about 281 households per 2012 DUSIB data, was covered with large white and purple sheets on the night of September 10 to hide it from foreign dignitaries, residents said. Ten-foot curtains along Nelson Mandela Marg and Munirka Marg restrict entry and exit to two points; residents said a similar cover-up with green curtains occurred during the 2023 G-20 Summit and complained that sanitation workers living there were being hidden rather than helped.

items.headline: India must give BRICS moral leadership and strategic clarity: Cong.
items.gist: The Congress urged the Indian government to take moral leadership of BRICS and use its chairmanship to restore the diplomatic stature India historically commanded as a voice of the Global South. Former Union Minister Salman Khurshid, who heads the party's foreign affairs department, said declarations of solidarity with the Global South must be matched by consistent action, citing concerns over perceived endorsement of attacks on BRICS member Iran, the government's limited diplomatic role in the West Asia war, and inadequate support for founding member South Africa; he said India should provide moral leadership as Manmohan Singh had while safeguarding national interests.

items.headline: PM holds series of bilateral meetings; hails India-UAE ties
items.gist: Prime Minister Narendra Modi said after meeting Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan that strong India-UAE ties are a symbol of stability during a time of uncertainty in West Asia, with discussions covering the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor and investment opportunities including L'Imad, the UAE's newest sovereign investment fund. The External Affairs Ministry said the leaders reviewed the UAE International Holding Company's announcement of an $11.5 billion investment in an integrated greenfield aluminium project in Odisha, expected to position Odisha as a global aluminium manufacturing hub.
items.paragraph: Prime Minister Narendra Modi said after meeting Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan that strong India-UAE ties are a symbol of stability during a time of uncertainty in West Asia, with discussions covering the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor and investment opportunities including L'Imad, the UAE's newest sovereign investment fund. The External Affairs Ministry said the leaders reviewed the UAE International Holding Company's announcement of an $11.5 billion investment in an integrated greenfield aluminium project in Odisha, expected to position Odisha as a global aluminium manufacturing hub. Mr. Modi also held bilateral meetings with Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed Ali, reviewing progress in economic cooperation, defence and security, and capacity building; with Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, who conveyed Malaysia's concurrence to establishing an Indian Consulate General in Kota Kinabalu, Sabah; and with Vietnamese Prime Minister Le Minh Hung, reviewing ties elevated to an Enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership during President To Lam's May 2026 visit to India.

items.headline: How Delhi is managing air traffic during the summit
items.gist: Behind the ceremonial welcomes for BRICS leaders lies a tightly coordinated aviation operation involving around 35 special aircraft, multiple airports, controlled airspace, and carefully timed movements to accommodate foreign dignitaries without disrupting Delhi's regular commercial flights. items.headline: Rapid Himalayan erosion triggers hidden source of CO2: study
items.gist: A study by researchers from IISER Pune, the Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology, and IIT-Roorkee published in Chemical Geology suggests that in glacier-fed river catchments of the upper Indus basin, CO2 release from pyrite oxidation may be three times higher than CO2 uptake by silicate weathering, with steep mountainous regions acting as net CO2 sources while flatter floodplains downstream remain sinks. As Himalayan glaciers crush rocks and expose pyrites to air and water, sulphides oxidise to sulphuric acid that reacts with carbonate rocks to release CO2, meaning glacier-driven erosion may influence long-term carbon cycles and contribute to climate warming over million-year timescales even as silicate weathering has helped cool the earth over the last 50 million years.

items.headline: Study finds far fewer genes truly linked to cerebral palsy
items.gist: A new study in The American Journal of Human Genetics found that of 515 candidate genes reported across 21 published genomic diagnostic studies involving 5,440 individuals diagnosed with cerebral palsy, rigorous statistical analysis could confirm a true association for only 89, and in a cohort of 460 patients sequenced across the Shriners Children's hospital network, stricter proof whittled 60 disease-causing mutations down to 16 genes. In India, where three in every 1,000 live births are affected by cerebral palsy and genetic testing is a rapidly growing field, acting on false alarms from standard panels can divert resources from effective treatments, while distinguishing true genetic mimics from coincidental mutations can connect families to precise care faster.

items.headline: Why are bank employees striking despite the PLI pause?
items.gist: The United Forum of Bank Unions called a nationwide strike on September 11 to protest a revised performance-linked incentive scheme announced in November 2024 that applies only to Scale IV officers and above, allowing up to 365 days of basic pay based on individual performance rather than the uniform 15 days basic pay plus dearness allowance formula for the rest of the workforce and departing from a 2020 agreement linking PLI to overall bank performance. Despite the government putting the PLI on hold after a September 8 meeting with a delegation led by the Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh, unions proceeded with the strike because there was no progress on their demand for a five-day work week and other unresolved issues including uniform dearness allowance for pensioners and an NPS-to-OPS switch option.

The strike disrupted branch banking for four days across many regions as it fell before the second Saturday, Sunday and Ganesh Chaturthi holidays, and unions have threatened a three-day strike from September 28 to 30 and a continuous indefinite strike from October 26 if demands remain unaddressed.

items.headline: Why has the Census been deferred in Manipur?
items.gist: The Centre deferred Census operations in Manipur on August 31 amid demands from several community-based and civil society organisations to first conduct the State's National Register of Citizens exercise with 1951 as the base year, following Union Home Minister Amit Shah's meeting with the Governor and Chief Minister as the State heads toward Assembly elections less than a year away. Meiteis, Meitei Pangals and Nagas opposed the Census while the Kuki-Zo Council supported it, fearing respectively that an NRC with a 1951 base year could unfairly exclude Kukis or that Census without NRC would skew delimitation and representation in the ethnically divided State where conflict since May 2023 has claimed almost 300 lives and displaced more than 62,000 people.

items.gist: China Southern Airlines announced it will resume regular passenger services on the Guangzhou-New Delhi route from September 21, restarting the service after a six-year suspension and operating more than 100 weekly flights across eight round-trip routes in South Asia. items.headline: A village with no people
items.gist: In just 10 years, Gattumeedapalle in Annamayya district of Andhra Pradesh has emptied out into a ghost village after repeated crop failures and depleting groundwater forced nearly 300 acres of groundnut cultivation and the community itself to wither away. Located about 125 km from Tirupati, the village that once sprawled across nearly 1,000 acres saw families gradually move to Kosuvaripalle or nearby Madanapalle from 2015 onward, leaving behind locked houses, abandoned furniture and electronic items that were looted including a temple bell, while former farmer Thimmakkagari Subbi Reddy, now a shepherd, says he has written off the village permanently.

items.headline: PIO missing in Nepal; help denied as he holds Indian passport: UK MP
items.gist: Dr Anirban Bhattacharyya, 66, a Newcastle University research associate who has lived in Britain for more than 60 years, remains on Nepal Police's missing-persons list over two weeks after Nepal's Aug 26 floods, with his constituency MP Ian Lavery alleging authorities declined to assist because he holds an Indian rather than British passport. Bhattacharyya was travelling with Kolkata-based Chalo Jaai Travel Club on a Kailash Mansarovar pilgrimage handled in Nepal by Samrat Tours and Travels and is among 32 contingent members still missing near Timure-Rasuwagadhi.

items.headline: Brics bridges Iran-UAE gulf, clears way for jt declaration
items.gist: Brics members agreed on a 140-paragraph New Delhi Declaration after intensive negotiations until 4am Saturday, overcoming sharp UAE-Iran differences over the West Asia conflict through a rare leader-level meeting between Iran President Masoud Pezeshkian and Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan. India played a key role in building consensus, with the declaration expressing serious concerns over attacks on civilian infrastructure and IAEA-safeguarded nuclear facilities, backing India's call for zero tolerance on terrorism including condemnation of the 2025 Pahalgam attack that killed 26 people, and seeking mechanisms to extradite fugitives and recover assets.

items.headline: Global South must shape, not just follow, rules: PM
items.gist: Opening the 18th Brics leaders' summit, PM Narendra Modi said UN Security Council reforms cannot be delayed and the "pyramid of privilege" in global governance must become a "platform of partnership," proposing that Brics draft 10 proposals for global governance reform. He said the Global South "stands in the front row of global crises, but in the back row of decision-making" and urged the bloc to turn developing countries from rule-takers to rule-shapers through economic integration.

items.headline: SIR NOTICE? HERE IS WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW
items.gist: The Special Intensive Revision claims and notices period from Aug 24 to Oct 22 covers 43.8 lakh voters asked to provide documents establishing place and date of birth, with 7 lakh people having completed hearings by Friday; Pearl D'Souza outlines nine case studies of common verification problems and acceptable documents. Cases include missing 2002 enumeration details resolved with electoral-roll extracts, Aadhaar and passports; father-name mismatches addressed with markscards, birth certificates and family passports; maiden-name changes proved with marriage records; and misspelt names in the 2002 roll confirmed through passport and Aadhaar.

items.headline: Brics calls for uninterrupted energy flow, infra protection
items.gist: Amid disruptions to global energy supplies, Brics leaders have called for uninterrupted flows of energy from diverse sources and stronger protection of critical energy infrastructure, including cross-border infrastructure, while stressing the continuing role of fossil fuels in the global energy mix. The declaration said energy security was a "crucial foundation for social and economic development, national security and the welfare of all nations," highlighted the need to enhance energy security by ensuring energy market stability and maintaining undisrupted flows from diverse sources, and recognised the continuing role of hydrocarbons while backing greater cooperation on smart grids, energy storage and critical minerals; the emphasis comes amid heightened risks around the Strait of Hormuz and possible disruption of Bab el-Mandeb by Iran-backed Houthis.

items.headline: ECONOMIC POWER OF BRICS
items.gist: World Bank data for 2025 show Brics members' GDP at $19,498 billion (China), $3,956 billion (India), $2,561 billion (Russia), $2,280 billion (Brazil), $1,446 billion (Indonesia), $1,277 billion (Saudi Arabia), $552 billion (UAE), $475 billion (Iran), $427 billion (South Africa), $365 billion (Egypt) and $126 billion (Ethiopia), with per capita GDP (PPP$) ranging from $79,344 (UAE) and $73,784 (Saudi Arabia) to $3,622 (Ethiopia); poverty head count ratios at $3 per day in 2021 PPP include 0% (China), 5.3% (India), 17.4% (South Africa) and 38.6% (Ethiopia). China and India together command nearly 70% of the total Brics economic weight in PPP terms; GDP and per capita GDP figures for UAE and Iran are for 2024.

items.headline: In denouncement of western bloc, Brics hits out at unilateral sanctions and tariff
items.gist: Brics slammed unilateral sanctions and tariff and non-tariff measures initiated by countries, arguing they distorted trade and were inconsistent with global trade rules — a statement seen aimed at the US, where Donald Trump has resorted to raising import duties including reciprocal tariffs declared illegal by the US Supreme Court, with the US still maintaining 10–12.5% tariff on over 50 nations using section 301 powers. The New Delhi Declaration also raised concern over "unilateral sanctions and secondary sanctions" amid US threats over oil purchases from Russia, Iran or Venezuela, noting India faced 50% additional American tariff including 25% "secondary tariffs" for purchasing Russian crude, and hit out at protectionism under the guise of environmental objectives; it backed practical solutions for cross-border payments among Brics countries, reform of World Bank and IMF, development-oriented WTO agriculture negotiations, and expressed strong condemnation of the Pahalgam terrorist attack while calling for halting policies aimed at forced displacement of Palestinians from Gaza despite the Oct 2025 ceasefire agreement.

items.headline: Brics opposes trade steps like EU carbon border tax
items.gist: Brics nations Saturday opposed unilateral trade measures such as the EU's carbon border adjustment mechanism (CBAM), which entered its operational regime on Jan 1 and imposes a border tax on carbon-intensive goods like iron and steel, aluminium and cement entering the 27 EU nations, saying such punitive, discriminatory and protectionist measures undermine developing countries' climate efforts and are not in line with international law. The New Delhi Declaration recognised the need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions while seeking to delink unilateral punitive action from climate goals, calling for actions based on equity and common but differentiated responsibilities, and highlighted the need to maintain undisrupted flows of energy from diverse sources including fossil fuels — four Brics members, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Iran and UAE, are among major global exporters of fossil fuel.

items.headline: Summit success gives BJP a boost
items.gist: India’s success in getting BRICS countries with conflicting outlooks—including on West Asia—to back a joint declaration comes as a timely domestic boost for BJP ahead of a month-long public-connect campaign from PM Modi’s birthday on Sept 17. BJP president Nitin Nabin said Bharat has again demonstrated commitment to a more representative world order, declaring “Bharat Leads BRICS 2026” and that the Global South gains a stronger voice.

items.headline: Caste identity alone can't invoke SC/ST Act: HC
items.gist: Allahabad HC held that Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe status alone cannot attract SC/ST Act provisions unless all essential ingredients of the offence are proved, quashing SC/ST charges against Raju Kuraihi and four others in a Ghaziabad property-sale dispute where the Act was invoked solely because the complainant was SC. Justice Santosh Rai said the Loni police FIR and case diary showed no caste-based words or humiliation on account of the victim’s SC/ST status.

items.headline: Five killed as van plunges into ditch
items.gist: Five people died when their van collided with an Arunachal Pradesh-registered truck on NH-15 at Tubukijhar in Assam’s Sonitpur district around midnight Friday; the van tumbled into a roadside ditch, was mangled beyond recognition and occupants were trapped until rescue teams extricated the bodies. The truck driver fled but was arrested later.

items.headline: Jarange's 5-day Mum march to clash with Chauti
items.gist: Rejecting Maharashtra govt appeals to defer protests during Ganesh Chaturthi, Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange announced a five-day march from Antarwali Sarati (Jalna) to Mumbai’s Azad Maidan for an indefinite hunger strike from Sept 20, with a first halt at Beed’s Patoda on Sept 16—suggesting a Sept 15 start and ~100 km daily legs. The march is expected to overlap the 10-day Ganesh festival from Sept 14; Jarange urged non-violent, disciplined participation with no stone-pelting or arson.

items.headline: Delayed Tax Payment Alone Not Wilful Evasion / HC junks tax evasion case against fashion designers
items.gist: Bombay HC on Sept 10 quashed I-T criminal proceedings against Abu Jani, Sandeep Khosla and their Andheri-based company over delayed 2017-18 tax payment, holding “mere failure to pay or delayed payment cannot be equated to wilful evasion.” The firm declared Rs 15.2 lakh income; Rs 5.27 lakh tax was payable after deductions. It paid Rs 5.27 lakh three days after an Oct 16, 2018 show-cause notice; I-T later sought Rs 1 lakh interest and filed a Sept 2019 complaint under sections 276C(2) and 278B.

items.headline: 'Reaction to a fall is not kissing': Man gets 1-yr jail
items.gist: A Mumbai sessions court sentenced 34-year-old cleaner Ritesh Armulla to one year’s rigorous imprisonment for forcibly kissing a Borivli (W) mall saleswoman twice on Sept 17, 2025, rejecting his claim he accidentally slipped and fell onto her. The court held a natural reaction to falling would not involve kissing, finding him guilty of criminal force and unwelcome physical contact with explicit sexual overtones after a two-month trial.

items.headline: IPO needs majority nod from nominee directors
items.gist: RBI’s Sept 11 letter on Tata Sons’ IPO continuation is expected at the Sept 17 board meeting, upending Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata’s effort to keep the company private and strengthening Shapoorji Pallonji Group chairman Shapoor Mistry (18.4% stake), who has pushed for listing. Under Article 121A, an IPO needs majority approval from Tata Trusts nominees Noel Tata and Venu Srinivasan; with Srinivasan publicly backing listing and Noel opposed, a 1-1 tie would leave Tata Sons chairman with the casting vote.

items.headline: BRICS meet calls for max restraint in West Asia
items.gist: The BRICS on Saturday called for maximum restraint in West Asia, expressed serious concern over deliberate attacks on civilian infrastructure and peaceful IAEA-safeguarded nuclear facilities, and urged respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity without assigning blame, as diplomats bridged differences between Iran and Saudi Arabia and the UAE overnight to adopt the New Delhi Declaration at the 18th summit hosted by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at Bharat Mandapam. On Israel-Palestine, BRICS invoked ICJ proceedings, reaffirmed support for Palestinian rights and a two-state solution based on 1967 borders, and Modi said the declaration provides clear direction that must be translated into tangible results.
